items.title: Final Fantasy XIV’s latest patch basically starts Evercold, but only gives you a short taste
items.content:
I know I said last time we’ve officially entered Evercold, but you can take that statement even more literally with patch 7.56. The MSQ for this patch is short but sweet, taking the Warrior of Light, Alphinaud, and Estinien to the fourth. There, we’re trapped on a deserted island, attacked by some strange machines, and saved by what is no doubt a teaser for the new ranged job to be revealed at the Tokyo Fan Fest. I won’t spoil it here, but it looks cool even if it isn’t exactly what I wanted. (I wanted something using Vanille’s whip staff thing from FFXIII, but maybe next time.) There’s unfortunately no dungeon or trial this time around, just two instanced battles, but both are a good time and interesting enough to engage you. The outfit you get at the end of the MSQ this time is also fantastic, and I’ve been using it as my Beastmaster outfit.

The focus of my time with this patch instead has been squarely on Beastmaster, the new Limited Job. As one of the few who love playing Blue Mage, I was stoked to have something similar again, and it seems a lot more people are enjoying this new job than did Blue Mage. That’s for good reason, as Beastmaster seems to focus way more on solo, open-world content instead of needing to go through party finder to get a group together for a dungeon. There is still some of that here, but most of the monsters you can tame are out in Eorzea.

More than anything, it’s nice to have something to do in these old zones again. I’ve been hunting down monsters to add to my besti-beastiery, fighting random mobs for experience, and running FATEs with other random players. That part alone is a lot of fun, but Beastmaster has its own unique gameplay style unlike any other job, even back when Summoner was actually a pet class. The basic loop for Beastmaster has you summon one of your three chosen monsters, then you and your companion attack an enemy to build up your respective TP bars. Once one of you reaches 100 TP, you can use a special color-coded attack, which will then reset your TP back to 0. Every monster only has one color attack, while you have all four at your disposal. To do some real damage, you need to follow up the first attack with the next in the sequence, shown going clockwise on your job gauge. So if you do a green move, your monster needs to use red, for example. Either one of you can start or end the combo too, but you still need to go in clockwise order to gain any bonus effects.

You’re not just waiting around to build up these combos, as there’s still a lot to consider in the moment-to-moment combat, even if it is overall slower-paced than the typical jobs in the game. When summoning a monster to the field, you gain the One with Nature buff, which allows you to use either Borrow or Tempered Release. Borrow lets you gain a special action based on the monster’s species for the duration they are on the field, while Tempered Release has your monster perform their unique skill. You can only use one per summon, so you need to choose wisely. You might want to borrow a cool dodge move that also grants you evasion up for a bit to dodge some incoming AoEs, or you might want your monster’s special healing skill for some more survivability overall. It’s a cool system even if it’s difficult to keep track of all the moving parts.

That difficult to keep track of theme continues in Beastmaster’s special solo content, the Crucible of the Unbroken. This is something of a rogue-like mode, where you move between spaces on a board game, with each space representing an encounter. You can pick a number of Beasties to join you on a board, but again, only three per battle, and all HP persists between encounters. You need to consider what monsters in your party will do the most damage or be the most survivable, when to use special items that grant healing, revives, or special buffs, and what temporary equipment you want to equip. It’s kind of a lot, but having only gone through the first board so far, it's a lot of fun too.

Overall, I’ve been having a blast with Beastmaster. While it can be a bit tedious to level at times, I’d prefer this be something that lasts me a good long while rather than speeding to the current cap of level 50. This’ll probably hold me over until Evercold at least, which is great because I just got all my other jobs to cap after my raiding group disbanded amicably, and I need things to do. Hope you enjoyed the read, and I’ll see you again next patch.

items.title: Wisdom of Nym: Future weapons for Final Fantasy XIV jobs in the ranged damage category
10 Best Final Fantasy Games According to Critics' Scores
items.summary: Come see which Final Fantasy titles critics love most, though you probably already know.
items.content:
By Murillo Zerbinatto Published Sep 19, 2026, 10:30 AM EDT Murillo Zerbinatto is an Editor at DualShockers specializing in JRPGs, RPGs, reviews, guides, and lists. He has been writing professionally since 2018 and covering games since 2020, with previous work published at Xfire , RPGInformer , IndieGameCulture , and GameRant .

A longtime JRPG enthusiast, Murillo has played more than 250 JRPGs and earned over 100 platinum trophies , giving him deep hands-on experience with the genre’s progression systems, side content, collectibles, and completionist challenges. His coverage often focuses on franchises such as Final Fantasy , Dragon Quest , Trails , Tales of , and Star Ocean .

Final Fantasy is one of the world's most famous franchises . It's about to complete 40 years of history, an incredible feat even for the most well-known brands. In all these years, the mainline entries have proven to be chameleon-like, with each showcasing its own setting, cast, gameplay system, and novelties, which worked out well for some but poorly for others.

To be honest, I am quite a fanboy of the series and generally like everything Square Enix throws my way. The nostalgia of seeing the same elements and mythology spread across every title is already enough to captivate me, regardless of whether it is a turn-based or action game. Just pitch in a chocobo, and I am satisfied.

The time has come to discover the franchise of the crystals.

However, that doesn't happen to everyone. Some clearly prefer the old-school Final Fantasy entries, while others appreciate the path Square has taken. To illustrate, I will list the 10 best Final Fantasy games by critics' scores. I won't limit this list to mainline titles, so expect to see spin-offs, remakes, remasters, and more.

To create the list, I avoided repeats and checked Metacritic critic scores because OpenCritic doesn't cover older Final Fantasy games.

Expand Collapse As someone who effusively prefers the first Final Fantasy Tactics and has a huge difficulty accepting the Judge system as a good mechanic, even though I love how it forces me to innovate every time, it is surreal to think that Final Fantasy Tactics Advance scored higher than its predecessor originally. But alas, here we are, and I concur it is still a pretty good strategy JRPG to play, even by today's standards.

One thing I like about FFTA compared to its predecessor is the sidequest and unlockables system, which is much more organized and intimate. On the other hand, the main story doesn't hold a candle to the political intrigue in Ivalice, and it is a bit more childish than I would have liked. Yet, I had fun, I dedicated dozens of hours to the game, and I came to dislike Marche at the end because, you know, who wouldn't want to be isekai-ed into a Final Fantasy world and become a Dragoon, right? Oh yeah, I am not a bangaa... dammit.

Expand Collapse Final Fantasy XVI carried a responsibility weighed down by Graviga. After the financially successful but critically divisive Final Fantasy XV , Square Enix had to get this one right. They got the most famous developer at the time, my lovely Naoki Yoshida, who saved Final Fantasy XIV and granted Square tons of profit, and also went back to the roots of a high fantasy setting with crystals at the forefront, a marketing strategy much like Final Fantasy IX , I would say.

I loved the game. The actors and performances were completely insane. The set pieces were out of this world, and the Eikon battles are among the best spectacles I have ever seen in entertainment media, with Bahamut's fight living rent-free in my mind. Still, I can see why some fans didn't enjoy Final Fantasy XVI as much. The combat is fine, but it lacks some strategic elements and, dare I say, the RPG factor. I will never get over the fact that I could kill a Bomb by spamming Fire, you know? But it is what it is. Considering the legacy of the crystals, I would say Square did fine work.

Final Fantasy Wiki Final Fantasy 7 RPG 8.2 /10

Expand Collapse Here we are, the one that conquered them all. If I had a nickel for every time I heard someone say they were introduced to the JRPG world via Final Fantasy VII , I would be a gazillionaire. Nothing wrong with that, because that is the legacy and praise FFVII carries and will carry forevermore. But since the game isn't even in my top 5 favorite FF titles, the discourse gets a bit exhausting after hearing it is the finest game ever for, like... the 873rd time.

But I understand, truly! Final Fantasy VII is a masterpiece and deserves all the kudos. My brother and I had to play the game three times to finally understand the whole Cloud and Zack plot (we were way too young!), while still managing to understand its gameplay systems because it was and still is easy to play and endearingly creative. It's no wonder Square decided to do a full-on remake of the title, turning it into a trilogy that will, hopefully, take the series to new heights and a new long-lasting audience.

items.title: Final Fantasy 14 Is Bringing Back a Fan-Favorite Crossover for the First Time in Over Two Years
items.summary: Finally, another chance to get one of the best mounts in Square Enix's MMO
items.content:
By Willa Rowe Published Sep 18, 2026, 2:01 PM EDT Willa Rowe is a contributing writer at Polygon, covering games and entertainment. She is a New York-based journalist and critic whose work has been featured in Kotaku, Digital Trends, the A.V. Club, GamesRadar+, and more. She also co-hosts the Girl Mode podcast. News Finally, another chance to get one of the best mounts in Square Enix's MMO

Y'shtola is featured prominently in the Final Fantasy XIV: Shadowbringers trailer. Image: Square Enix Final Fantasy 14 Sign in to your Polygon.com account Add Us Summary Generate a summary of this story Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Thread Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap It's official, Noctis is returning to Eorzea. Square Enix has officially announced that the Nocturne for Heroes event will once again be available in Final Fantasy 14 for a limited time. Players last experienced the Final Fantasy 15 crossover in 2024.

Warriors of Light can pick up the quest that begins the crossover starting on Sept. 24, 2026 at 1:00 a.m. PDT. You'll have just a few weeks to complete it and collect all of the collaboration's rewards, as the event concludes on Oct. 13, 2026 at 7:59 a.m. PDT. The Nocturne for Heroes event first ran in 2021 and returned in 2024, so don't expect that you'll be able to play it again anytime soon after this year's revival concludes. The quest line for the event sees the Warrior of Light aiding Noctis, the protagonist of Final Fantasy 15 .

Players can start the event by picking up the quest "The Man in Black" from Kipih Jakkya in Ul'dah near the Steps of Nald. If you've previously completed the quests, you can speak to the NPC to use the seasonal event replay feature. You won't be able to start the event unless you have a character that is level 50, and you've completed the main scenario quest, "The Ultimate Weapon."

It seems like somebody didn’t get the memo Square Enix via Polygon There will, of course, be plenty of limited-time items to collect during the event. The hottest item will be the Regalia Type-G mount , which continues to be one of the MMO's best mounts. It'll cost 200,000 MGP from the Ironworks Vendor. But that won't be the only reward to grab. Here's a full list of items and how to get them.

If this isn't your first time doing the event, you might try playing it on the Switch 2; It may unexpectedly be the best place to play the MMO .

Congrats on beating Dancing Mad (Ultimate), it was easier before patch 7.55

items.title: Next Final Fantasy FFXIV Crossover Brings FFXV Back
items.summary: Noctis from FFXV will back in FFXIV for a time thanks to the return of a limited-time crossover event quest.
items.content:
FFXIV will get content from another Final Fantasy game again thanks to a rerun of the FFXV crossover. Square Enix announced that will kick off next week on September 24, 2026. This run of A Nocturne for Heroes is identical to the event that first debuted back in April 2019 , so there’s nothing new if you already met Noctis Lucis Caelum. However, this does mark the first time the event appeared since the launch of the Switch 2 release.

As usual, the requirements for the questline that begins with “ The Man in Black ” are a bit high compared to some of these crossovers or special events. You must get your character to level 50 and have finished the A Realm Reborn main scenario quest “The Ultimate Weapon.” If you have, then Kipih Jakkya will be at Ul’dah, Steps of Nald at X:8.5, Y:9.7. This starts a three-quest storyline that results in someone getting the Regalia Type-G mount and the Lucian Prince’s armor set that features boots, bottoms, a fingerless glove, and a jacket. Someone can also unlock Noctis’ Lucian Locks Modern Aesthetics hairstyle for finishing it.

Here’s the original trailer that goes over the event.

This marks the fourth time we’ve seen this FFXV crossover quest in FFXIV . Following the 2019 debut, it returned in 2021 and 2024 as well. This also means that this time every single platform the game is on will get a chance to go over it again.

Final Fantasy XIV is available for the Switch 2, PS4, PS5, Xbox Series X, and PC. Final Fantasy XV is on the PS4, Xbox One, and PC via the standard version and Switch, PS4, Xbox One, PC, and mobile devices via the Pocket Edition. The FFXIV FFXV crossover event returns between September 24, 2026 and October 13, 2026.

items.title: Final Fantasy 14 relaxes guidelines for non-commercial fan-made merch. New rules prohibit use of generative AI and 3D printing
items.summary: The update to FFXIV's Materials Usage License comes with several additions related to physical fan-made goods.
items.content:
Home News Final Fantasy 14 relaxes guidelines for non-commercial fan-made merch. New rules prohibit use of generative AI and 3D printing The update to FFXIV's Materials Usage License comes with several additions related to physical fan-made goods.

News 2026-09-18 19:41 Akira Sada In an official post on The Lodestone, the community site for Final Fantasy XIV , Square Enix recently announced an update to its “Materials Usage License,” which governs how fans can use FFXIV’s content.

The rules now grant permission for fans to create non-commercial physical goods under certain conditions, which was previously not allowed. Of note, the new guidelines also explicitly prohibit the creation of physical items using AI-generated derivative works or 3D printing.

Under the new terms of use, fan-made physical merch using copyrighted material of FFXIV must be made personally, with new restrictions including but not limited to necessitating a link (or QR code) of the new policy be made available on said goods (instead of a simple copyright text). Fan-made creations also must be made free of charge if given to others, as the guideline strictly forbids any sales or commercial use of its IP.

Notably, the commissions of physical items have an exception, namely for business cards and stickers. While the guideline prohibits the commissioning of companies or stores to create other printed products, these two are given a pass under certain conditions. Business cards require the player’s character, Home World (server) and/or social media tag to be present somewhere in the design. Stickers, on the other hand, may only be printed if the design is of an illustration or screenshot that includes the player’s own character.

The new policy also hammers the point that depictions that imitate preexisting official FFXIV merchandise are forbidden, giving examples such as “creating items by molding official merchandise or promotional items.”

The business-card exception may be of particular interest to FFXIV fans who exchange character or community cards at real-world events such as Fan Festival, although Square Enix has not stated that this was the reason for the exception.

items.title: Final Fantasy XIV: Complete Edition for Nintendo Switch 2 Review
items.summary: FINAL FANTASY XIV Online Complete Edition is perfect for new players as it includes the base game and all expansions through Dawntrail.
items.content:
Final Fantasy XIV released on the Switch 2 as of a few weeks ago (depending on date of publication). I bought the Complete Edition , which gives access through Dawntrail … without knowing about the impending free trial version due out on August 4th. Still, I got 2 months+ worth of playtime to work with before having to get a Switch 2-specific subscription. So, how does it fare so far just after the A Realm Reborn expansion? Let’s find out!

Now, if you’re a Switch 2 newbie (like I am), then a lot of what is mentioned here will appear overwhelming to you, especially the plot of A Realm Reborn . Though, don’t worry, you do not need to play FFXIV 1.0 to understand FFXIV: A Realm Reborn ’s story, though having prior knowledge will help in understanding the context of certain flashbacks.You see, those masked individuals working with the Ixal (if your hometown is New Gridinia, more on that later) and in mysterious flashback cutscenes detailing the Primal Bahamut Dalahmud Moon that brought about the end of 1.0 are Ascions, aka: Paragons.

Their ability to summon creatures and possess people comes into play throughout A Realm Reborn and later expansions, and if you stick with it through all this story (there’s so much and constantly more coming into 2027 and beyond with Evercold ), you’ll discover the conflict between the Ascions and the Scions of the Seventh Dawn, with so many implications and events following these that I DARE not spoil. Yda and Papalymo are the first two story-significant characters you’ll meet, as a heads-up.

One of the downsides of Final Fantasy XIV: Complete Edition on Switch 2 is the need to pay a separate subscription fee entirely separate from the NOT-REQUIRED Switch Online. Yeah, in addition to needing any version of the game to play, nearly 150 GBs on space on your internal storage or MicroSD Express card, you also need a SEPARATE subscription to play the game past the free month grace period on Switch 2!! Yes, it’s annoying. Does it take away from the fun I am having right now? Hmm… a little. Thankfully, paying that fee is a bit easier than I thought. Just use the Nintendo eShop.

The game shines with its Xenoblade Chronicles -esque approach to combat. Each attack is on a cooldown after use. The more beneficial an attack or buff is, the longer it takes to recharge. Which attack you follow up with in combat after the previous one can offer benefits like increased damage to an enemy, for example, with the Lancer\Dragoon’s True Thrust following the use of a vorpal blade.

On the performance side of the gameplay, when dealing with less than 8 NPCs in one area at a time, like in a city or overworld, the FPS is generally 60, for BOTH docked and handheld (I don’t care about FPS as long as it’s stable and PLAYABLE). In the city or certain intense areas, the FPS is at a steady 30.

The music as always is excellent. the theme that capped off 1.0, known as “Answers”, is the most beautiful and best song in the entire franchise. Playing mainly in the raid dungeon known as The Unending Coil of Bahamut (Ultimate)’s final battle against Primal Bahamut, this song is masterclass in orchestral majestic bliss, and so on and so forth. I have listened to it about 50 times so far, with each time better than the last. It also plays at one other important point in the expansions that I, again, DARE not spoil, by the way.

And there’s so much more I even haven’t gotten into. Side quests, Raid Battles, FATE Battles, Team compositions for Raid dungeons, Parties, etc. AND, lastly, did I mention I’m STILL on the first expansion ( A Realm Reborn )?! I’m just now checking out the other two towns and their overworlds as part of the larger quest. AND I still have SIX more expansions after this to get through! There’s certainly a LOT of content here, which I can appreciate, but there might be TOO MUCH for me to do in such a short time.

If you’re looking for a Xenoblade -type MMORPG with memorable characters and plenty of engaging story beats to keep you interested, this game will scratch that itch, and then some.

My one complaint is the number of expansions and the amount of story/side content is a bit too overbearing and hand-holdy at times. Other than that, I enjoyed my time with FFXIV and the realm of Eorzea, and I can’t wait to come back for another adventure with the Evercold expansion in 2027.

If you liked this review, be sure to check out my review on Legacy of Kain: Ascendance . Thanks for reading, and I’ll see you next time.

items.title: New ‘Final Fantasy 14’ Job Leaked on Square Enix’s Official Site
Square Enix reminds Final Fantasy XIV players that the Switch 2’s free subscription period is ending soon
items.summary: Square Enix posted an update on its official Final Fantasy XIV page today to remind players that the free one-month grace period for its long-running MMO on
items.content:
Square Enix posted an update on its official Final Fantasy XIV page today to remind players that the free one-month grace period for its long-running MMO on Switch 2 will be ending soon. Starting September 7th, 2026, players will either need to buy the “Starter” or “Complete” editions of the game, or switch over to the free-trial that limits access to certain features. If you’ve already purchased FFXIV on Switch 2, your included month of game access will take effect on September 8, 2026.

This can be a little confusing to those not familiar with MMOs, but Square Enix launched FFXIV on Switch 2 with 30 free days as a means of testing the server stability on Nintendo’s console. Technically speaking, the game doesn’t actually release until September 7th, so Square Enix wants to remind players that they’ll soon need to start paying to keep playing. MMO fees go towards server maintenance and the development of additional content, of which Final Fantasy XIV has received six major expansion packs, so this isn’t anything new. This announcement is merely a warning so that people aren’t caught off guard if they suddenly lose access.

In order to pay for access on Nintendo Switch 2, players will need to utilize FFXIV coins, as Square Enix calls them. This is a separate subscription from the PC, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X|S versions, though having dual subscriptions will net you a 50% discount for access on the Switch 2 port. Basically, you purchase coins ahead of time and use those to pay off the monthly fee. FFXIV coins can be purchased from the game’s launcher, which will redirect to the eShop for completion of the purchase. It seems a little convoluted, but I suppose Square Enix is trying to conform to standards set by Nintendo’s online ecosystem.

If you don’t want to deal with any of that, Final Fantasy XIV does have a rather generous free trial. You’re limited in certain aspects, such as losing the ability to form parties with other players, but you can otherwise experience the entirety of XIV’s story and even play through the first four expansions. It’s certainly a hell of a lot of content for the low price of $0.

The range features graphic hoodies, character tees, washed denim sets and Mothercrystal jewelry.

Launches September 16, 2026, via Tokyo pop-ups and Diesel online.

Diesel has teamed up with Square Enix ‘s acclaimed MMORPG Final Fantasy XIV for a multi-faceted project anchored in the shared philosophy of “BRAVE”.

Fusing fashion, gaming culture and contemporary art, the centerpiece of the project is a 27-piece capsule collection. The lineup translates rich gaming lore into streetwear staples, spanning washed denim jackets, wide-leg denim trousers, hoodies, long-sleeve tees, graphic T-shirts and silver jewelry. Design motifs draw directly from the world of Hydaelyn, featuring imagery of Azem’s Crystal, the Mothercrystal, the Grand Companies of Eorzea and iconic Scions of the Seventh Dawn characters including Y’shtola, Thancred, Alphinaud, and Estinien.

Ranging in price from ¥11,000 to ¥207,900 JPY (approx. $69 – $1,302 USD), the collection kicks off on September 16, 2026, with an exclusive pop-up at Isetan Shinjuku in Tokyo, which will offer custom job-icon embroidery services and a 30-set limited “Scions of the Seventh Dawn Complete Box”. A wider release follows on October 2, 2026, via Diesel’s official online store and the DIESEL SHIBUYA flagship, alongside secondary pop-ups at Hankyu Umeda in Osaka and Iwataya in Fukuoka later in the month. Coinciding with the drop, DIESEL ART GALLERY in Shibuya will host a collaborative collage art exhibition by renowned artist Kosuke Kawamura from October 2 through November 8, 2026. items.title: Review: Final Fantasy XIV on Nintendo Switch 2 is the best version of the game
items.content:
I have wanted to get back into Final Fantasy XIV for quite some time. I am a massive fan of everything it offers, from the art direction to the scope of the world and adventures that are held within it. I love the way that it handles narrative within the MMO format, and the massive range of locations to visit. I really, really love the music (I went to a FFXIV symphony and everything), and just generally the very Final Fantasy design of it.

Related reading: To think that I played this for the first time way back on the PlayStation 3. My thoughts back then.

But – and it’s a big but – Final Fantasy XIV is a MMO, and MMOs do demand a time commitment, both in terms of the raw hours you plug into it, and the frequency with which you need to play. Take a big break from an MMO, and it just becomes progressively more difficult to step back into.

I tried to get back into FFXIV once when I first picked up the ROG Xbox Ally . The device handled the game just lovely, but I’m not a frequent PC player, and so at some point I put the device down, took a long break, and just… let my subscription slip again.

I am, however, a frequent Nintendo Switch 2 player. By that I mean “daily”. And so now, with the game’s little icon sitting right there on my Switch 2 home screen, I’ve been logging in for at least a little playtime every day. I’ve already made significantly more progress than I did on the ROG.

Final Fantasy XIV plays just lovely on Switch 2, to start with that important point. The console’s screen is just large enough to be able to handle the very busy interface (it’s an MMO, it’s necessary) without distracting from the core action when you want to watch the fireworks. The game’s visual engine is just now ever-so-slightly showing its age with relatively primitive character models and textures – it has been going for something like 13 years at this point – but the art direction is still as stunning as ever, and I’ve loved revisiting my favourite parts of the world from my first playthrough.

Speaking of, I have started a totally fresh character and save file (I wouldn’t even be able to track down my original avatar from a decade ago, if she still exists on servers somewhere, even if I wanted to. I can’t remember my username, password, or the email address it was attached to). I love how it’s possible to play through all the base game and early expansions with NPCs, and not rely on parties of humans for the various dungeons. If you’ve ever played a FFXIV dungeon before, you’ll know that human allies tend to… well, race through it. One of the few unpleasant memories I have from my first playthrough of Final Fantasy XIV was getting to the very final dungeon of the base game and basically missing the whole thing (and being left behind) because I was trying to follow the story. The conclusion to literally dozens of hours of play.

Now, thanks to NPCs, you can enjoy most of the many expansions and all the stories within them at your own pace. And enjoy the typically excellent music, enemy layouts and dungeon design without feeling rushed, too. I even took time to take screenshots, which is one of my favourite ways to log my adventures in this game.

There is a downside, though. Because Square Enix wants to funnel players into the later expansions where, from their perspective, all the value to the players is, they’ve taken steps to streamline the earlier parts of the game, meaning that you accumulate experience points much (much) faster, and have to do far (far) fewer quests along the way. I have been exclusively undertaking the main quest line, with no side quests, let alone grinding, and my avatar is more than twice the minimum recommended level for any given quest or boss battle.

I understand why they did this, because otherwise it would be a truly intimidating, overwhelming task for a completely new player to get up to the newer expansions, but it means that those same players don’t get to spend enough time in parts of the world to really enjoy their contribution to the whole. The major cities are fine, but you’ll fly through little town areas where previously you’d spend a gaming session or two completing all the side quests. They’re barely blips and blink-and-you’ll-miss-them moments now, which really messes with the pacing for what was previously a truly wonderfully paced game that slowly walked you from one wonder to the next.

I don’t necessarily know what the solution is there, though if it were possible, I would have appreciated the option to toggle whether I wanted the accelerating levelling on or not.

Still, that’s my only gripe. The only other minor issue is that, when it comes to the chat, the Switch’s virtual keyboard doesn’t exactly allow for the same typing speed as a proper keyboard. I don’t even know if it’s possible to connect a Bluetooth keyboard to the Switch 2, as I haven’t tried yet, but even if it were possible, that would significantly undermine the portability of the experience. Currently I haven’t been social enough in FFXIV to require the chat function much, but I can see that becoming an issue later on in the game.

Those are only minor quibbles, obviously, set against a game that is hundreds upon hundreds of hours in scope, and now in an extremely portable and accessible format. FFXIV is a hobby all by itself, and now I can embrace and indulge it in full.

items.content:
Once more, a horde of Yo-kai descends upon Eorzea! Join in the fun and get your paws on weapons, mounts, a framer's kit, and minions─including Jibanyan and Whisper! This time around, the event features three new indoor furnishings: wibbly-wobbly Jibanyan, wibbly-wobbly Komasan, and wibbly-wobbly USApyon. * This event is identical to the one previously held, with the addition of three indoor furnishing items. * If you have already completed the quest for this event, it cannot be accepted again. However, you may still earn Yo-kai Medals while equipped with a Yo-kai Watch. * During the event, Yo-kai Watches will be available for purchase from recompense officers in major cities.

Event Duration

From Tuesday, August 4, 2026 at 1:00 a.m. (PDT) / 8:00 (GMT) / 9:00 (BST) / 18:00 (AEST) to Monday, October 5, 2026 at 7:59 a.m. (PDT) / 14:59 (GMT) / 15:59 (BST) / Tuesday, 6 October at 1:59 (AEDT) * Dates and times are subject to change.

How to Participate

Speak with the poor-heeled youth on the Steps of Nald (X:9.2 Y:9.1) in Ul'dah. Upon completion of the quest, you will receive a Yo-kai Watch and Yo-kai Medallium which you can use to obtain Yo-kai Medals. * Players must be level 15 and above to start the quest. * Players must have completed one of the following main scenario quests: "The Gridanian Envoy," "The Lominsan Envoy," or "The Ul’dahn Envoy."
